E03-01.en: A vast muddy brown river roaring under a heavy grey storm sky at dusk, a low wooden pontoon bridge on the far bank, and beyond it an endless black mass of Turkic cavalry campfires stretching to the horizon, wolf-head banners snapping in the wind

E03-02.en: A sea of Turkic steppe warlords' forward camp on the north bank of a wide river at dusk, thousands of fur-hooded cavalry silhouettes, rows of hide tents, tethered horses, cooking smoke, torchlight reflecting on muddy water

E03-03.en: A walled Tang dynasty capital's outer moat and gate under harsh noon light, Turkic horse archers galloping along the outside embankment, one archer drawing his bow mid-shot, arrows stuck in the wooden gate, defenders' silhouettes on the rampart above

E03-04.en: A completely empty early Tang capital city at dusk seen down a deserted main avenue, shut heavy gates, abandoned market stalls, not a single figure, dust and scattered leaves, oppressive silence

E03-05.en: A determined Tang prince in battered dark armor at dusk, swinging onto a warhorse at the head of exactly six mounted retainers, cloaks whipping, the wide empty city wall rising behind them, determination rather than bravado in his face

E03-06.en: A theatrical stage of a later-dynasty Chinese storytelling opera, a painted backdrop of an empty city bluff, a costumed actor gesturing with a long sleeve before a painted fan, gaudy lantern light, deliberately kitschy and romantic

E03-07.en: Close low-angle of a young Tang prince at a river bridge head at dusk, six horses behind him, jaw set and eyes hard, refusing to retreat, wind tearing at his cloak, the swollen river filling the background

E03-08.en: A low wooden bridge over a wide muddy river at dusk, six armored horses standing abreast with drawn sabers at the bridge head, a single Tang prince in front facing an unseen enemy across the water, dust and torch glow, absolute resolve

E03-09.en: An immense Turkic cavalry horde pressing across an open plain at dusk, tens of thousands of riders with fur and lamellar armor filling the horizon edge to edge, dust storm rising, a tiny lone Tang defensive line barely visible in the distance

E03-10.en: Two negotiating parties facing each other across a wide river at dusk on a low bridge, Tang retainers on the near side, Turkic leaders and banners on the far side, ropes and gifts of silk piled on the bridge deck, tense negotiation rather than battle

E03-11.en: A solemn oath ceremony on a low wooden bridge over a wide muddy river at dusk, a bound white warhorse kneeling at the rail with a blade laid across the mooring post beside it, torchlit witnesses in armor on both sides, silk ribbons and a deed unrolled on the boards, ritual and gravity, no blood shown, restrained and ceremonial

E03-12.en: A young Tang emperor alone in a dark tent at night, knuckles white on a rolled document, face carved tight with swallowed humiliation, a single candle, confiscated silk and gold chests visible behind him in shadow

E03-13.en: A lone Tang emperor sitting motionless by a single oil lamp at night, studying a crude enemy campaign map with a chess-like hand resting on the table, eyes calculating cold patience, absolute stillness that reads as contained rage

E03-14.en: A frozen northern steppe at first light three winters later, blizzard aftermath, dead and starving sheep and cattle half-buried in snow, scattered yurts, a broken cart axle, an abandoned cooking fire going out, desolation

E03-15.en: A catastrophic steppe winter disaster in the snow, a Turkic herding family sheltering under a collapsed hide tent, frozen cattle carcasses behind them, a woman wrapping a child, blowing snow reducing everything to white silence

E03-17.en: A grand early Tang palace hall lit by hundreds of candles and lanterns, an elderly emperor in imperial robes joyfully playing a pipa, a bound Turkic khan forced to whirl in an exotic steppe dance, hundreds of steppe chiefs kneeling in tribute, opulent and cruel

E03-18.en: An idealized prosperous Tang golden age fantasy in warm golden light, endless fertile fields and full granaries, laden ox carts, peaceful market with no beggars, abundant harvest, a deliberately romanticized golden-age vision

E03-19.en: A dim archive room, a thick household register ledger open on a bare wooden table, a single lamp raking across columns of tiny cramped brush characters, a tally of numbers, a cold accountant's still life

E03-20.en: Extreme close-up of brittle yellowed pages of an ancient Chinese institutional treatise's food-and-revenue chapter, columns of dense brush script, one column ringed in ink, pages curling at the edges, a scholar's fingertip holding the page

E03-21.en: The apex of Sui dynasty prosperity, a vast crowded early seventh century walled capital at noon, dense ranked rooftops and market streets packed with people, ox carts and porters, banners, an enormous living population implied

E03-22.en: Ten years of civil war aftermath, a field of bleached bones and broken weapons stretching to the horizon under a bleak grey sky, a single vulture, no living figure, silent devastation, silent famine

E03-23.en: A deserted early Tang village at dusk, roofless mud-brick houses, empty grain jars, weeds choking a collapsed courtyard gate, a broken hoe, no people at all, an entire county emptied

E03-24.en: A vast ruined plain where a thriving population once farmed, only stumps and ash drifts remain, cold wind, a distant empty road, the physical scale of sixty percent of a nation gone

E03-25.en: A hollowed-out imperial treasury vault in low light, opened chests with almost nothing inside, a few scattered coins, empty shelves where treasure should be, a lone official with a lamp realizing the vault is bare, the marrow of the empire scooped out

E03-26.en: A drought-stricken Guanzhong plain under a brutal white sun, a blank sky with no cloud at all, heat shimmer distorting the horizon, parched cracked earth, a farmer standing hopeless with an empty bucket

E03-27.en: Severe drought, a completely dried riverbed splitting into cracked mud, dead fish, a withered locust, cracked earth stretching away, fierce white light, no water anywhere

E03-28.en: A locust swarm blotting out the sun over a ruined farm village, dense churning insects filling the sky, a desperate family beating pots and waving cloth, stripped bare field behind, orange insect-filtered gloom, panic

E03-29.en: A queue of gaunt starving civilians at a temple wall for a thin grain ration, hollow-eyed mothers with infants, a village official ladling almost nothing, cracked earth, silent desperation, no violence yet

E03-30.en: An empty grain store in the palace, doors forced open, every bin turned over and empty, spilled chaff and dust, a stunned granary official holding a lamp, a locked official grain silo standing useless

E03-31.en: An emperor on a high throne dais at night dispatching desperate edicts, kneeling scribes below writing frantically, lamps low, a sealed edict about to be read out, the mechanics of a state admitting it cannot feed its people

E03-32.en: A long column of famine refugees trudging along a dusty road away from the capital, bundles on backs, hollow faces, an official handing out a travel pass certificate, a child dragging a cart, exodus

E03-33.en: A famine road outside the capital at dusk, a poor desperate couple handing over their own small child to a wealthier man in exchange for a bowl of rice gruel, the child's hand released, devastating, restrained not gory

E03-34.en: Sparse early Tang farmland slowly recovering, a few thin crops in tired fields, a single ox, a smallholding family working, far more empty land than planted, slow patient recovery after catastrophe

E03-35.en: A vision of the far-future Kaiyuan golden age a century later, a genuinely vast prosperous Tang capital, dense crowds, endless markets and canals, golden age finally achieved, contrasted with the sparse present

E03-36.en: A cramped treasury office at night, a single exhausted clerk surrounded by unpaid salary tallies and uncollected accounts, a bare coin string and an abacus, cabinets of unpaid bills, the state unable to pay itself

E03-37.en: The inner gate courtyard of a Tang imperial palace at first light immediately after a coup, the great vermilion doors standing open, toppled ceremonial braziers and a shattered arrow bundle scattered across the flagstones, a general's sword abandoned in the dust with its imperial tassel, absolute stillness and total absence of people, dawn light raking across the debris, the violence implied only by what remains

E03-38.en: The inner gate courtyard of an imperial palace at first light just after a violent coup, overturned ritual vessels, scattered weapons and a broken arrow shaft on the flagstones, an abandoned imperial seal lying in the dust, guards standing away in the far shadows, total silent absence, the violence implied only by what is left behind

E03-39.en: A Tang court official's desk with a carefully drafted legal proposal on institutional lending, an ingenious administrative device laid out in neat columns, lamp light, the paperwork of a desperate financial workaround

E03-40.en: Close-up of Tang legal codes and institutional statutes on bamboo and wood slips, an official finding the passage on official lending moneys and appointed money officers, a finger on the text, dense archaic legal script

E03-41.en: A state treasury official pushing heavy chests of coin out of a vault to be distributed to government offices, porters carrying chests down a corridor, string-of-cash counted, the principal being handed out as loans

E03-42.en: Several Tang government offices receiving their allotments of public coin, clerks counting heavy strings of cash onto desks in different rooms, a whole bureaucracy being funded by its own lending principal

E03-43.en: A bundle of government coin marked as loan principal, being converted into a merchant's hands as seed capital, a clerk writing an official money officer title, coins passing from state to private lender, the mother money

E03-44.en: A calculating money officer's abacus and a column of arithmetic for monthly four-percent interest, a hundred coins becoming four, then compounding, an official's careful hand, usurious arithmetic on old paper

E03-45.en: A money officer walking a busy street collecting interest from small borrowers, a desperate farmer handing over grain for a debt payment, the collector's tally stick, urban usury in a Tang market street

E03-46.en: A state hall where the central government openly functions as the empire's biggest moneylender, money officials seated with their ledgers taking public loans, a bitter irony conveyed by solemn official ritual around piles of coin

E03-47.en: An emperor alone at a low table at night, surrounded by unpayable accounts, staring at an abacus and unsent memorial, unable to touch the political settlement that supports his rule, the bitter fruit of a deadlock

E03-48.en: A victorious Tang prince in bloodstained armor at dusk on a battlefield, and superimposed behind him a cold shadow of fratricidal guilt, his face carrying the awareness of a legitimacy he has not earned

E03-49.en: A dissolute east palace crown prince in a dim pleasure palace, wine cups, silk cushions, a bored scowl, a cliched wastrel caricature, deliberately stagey and unflattering, the misleading legend

E03-50.en: The legitimate crown prince as an experienced field commander in the Hebei campaign, battered armour, captured rebel banners in the mud, mature and capable, resolute, genuinely impressive, not a buffoon

E03-51.en: A Tang prince as a pure military commander on campaign, strict discipline, review of a fortified position, a man comfortable in armour and not in court, cool professional command, the other half of the dynastic contradiction

E03-52.en: An imperial hand hovering over an official history scroll with a red cinnabar brush, the decision to alter the record visible in the hesitation, lamplight, the ethics of history in a single gesture

E03-53.en: An emperor facing an ironclad ancient rule that the sovereign may not read his own chronicles, an impassive court scholar stating the prohibition, the throne and the taboo between them, uncomfortable silence

E03-54.en: An emperor and a gaunt remonstrating minister in long tense confrontation across a court hall, seventeen years of confrontation implied, a wooden court tablet raised, the emperor's jaw set, reluctant respect

E03-55.en: A scholar formerly of the deposed crown prince being raised at court to high rank, an official appointment decree, the court watching a former enemy elevated, a bold political investment publicly performed

E03-56.en: A court hall where an emperor plants a banner of reconciliation, a former enemy minister standing honoured among hostile former supporters, a political signal made physical, officials reading the meaning

E03-57.en: A great court assembly of eastern aristocratic literati and former crown prince retainers, the newly enthroned emperor among them, former enemies now seated in his hall, the audience that must be persuaded

E03-58.en: A heavy golden collar locked around an emperor's own neck, forged from his own virtue, its clasp at his throat, a metaphor made physical, candlelit, the burden of proved righteousness

E03-59.en: An emperor forcing his own face into perfect composure in a lamplit inner hall, his hands pressed flat on a table, all the fury deliberately held down, the terrible discipline of tolerating the man who must correct him

E03-60.en: An ancient bloody blade reversing direction thirty years on, its edge turned back toward its owner's own chest, reflected in a dark polished surface, a night of reckoning, a dagger that has come home
